name: Learning from few examples and demonstrations
gist: Papers enabling robots to pick up new tasks from just one or two human demonstrations or examples—reducing the data burden for learning new behaviors.
explain: Ideally, a robot learns a new task from just one or two examples shown by a human. A person shows the robot how to stack blocks, and the robot can immediately stack blocks in any configuration it has not seen before. This kind of learning—from few examples, sometimes called few-shot learning—is common in humans. A child sees one person tie a shoe and can tie their own shoes. But for robots, this is extremely hard because the robot has to extract the essential structure of the task from very limited data, without overfitting to irrelevant details.

The challenge is generalization. If you show a robot one video of stacking a red block on a blue block, the robot might learn 'put red things on blue things.' But the underlying task is 'stack blocks on top of each other'—the colors do not matter. Or the task is 'place object A on top of object B' and you should generalize to any objects. How does the robot figure out what matters? With a thousand examples, the robot can see a pattern. With one example, the robot has to guess. The robot also has to transfer what it learned from one morphology (body shape) to another—if the robot saw a human hand demonstrating a task, can it do the same task with a robot hand? The human hand and robot hand are different, so direct imitation does not work.

Papers here use several strategies. Some use meta-learning—train the robot on many different tasks, so it learns how to learn. When shown one new task, it recognizes patterns from previous tasks and adapts quickly, because it has practiced the skill of adapting many times before. Some use language to help—a human says 'put the red block on the blue block,' and language gives the robot a hint about which features matter, because words pick out what is important from the infinite details in the scene. Some use video as raw data—a human demonstrates with their hand, and the robot learns to translate human hand motion into its own motion. Others use implicit representations: the robot does not learn 'do this action,' but rather learns to embed observations in a space where similar tasks cluster together. In that space, one or two examples are enough to find nearby tasks the robot has seen before, because the representation has already organized similar tasks close to each other.

papers.title: Difference-Aware Retrieval Polices for Imitation Learning
papers.contribution: DARP achieves consistent 15-46% performance improvements over standard behavior cloning across continuous control and robotic manipulation domains with different visual representations.

papers.title: Knowledge Diversion for Efficient Morphology Control and Policy Transfer
papers.contribution: Achieves 3.3× improvement in cross-task transfer sample efficiency and 16.7× model size reduction for single-agent deployment.

papers.title: MoMaGen: Generating Demonstrations under Soft and Hard Constraints for Multi-Step Bimanual Mobile Manipulation
papers.contribution: MoMaGen generates much more diverse datasets than previous methods for multi-step bimanual mobile manipulation, enabling successful imitation learning from generated data.

papers.title: Task Tokens: A Flexible Approach to Adapting Behavior Foundation Models
papers.contribution: Task Tokens reduces trainable parameters per task by up to 125x and converges up to 6x faster than standard baselines while enabling incorporation of user-defined priors.

papers.title: Time Optimal Execution of Action Chunk Policies Beyond Demonstration Speed
papers.contribution: RACE achieves up to a 4× acceleration over the original policy while maintaining high task success rates in both simulation and real-world robotic manipulation.

papers.title: Distinguishing Imitation Error from Intrinsic Motion Learning Difficulty
papers.contribution: TVS enables accurate error attribution: high error on low-TV motions indicates policy deficiency, while high error on high-TV motions reflects fundamental learning constraints; supports mocap quality control.

papers.title: Dynamics Are Learned, Not Told: Semi-Supervised Discovery of Latent Dynamics Geometries For Zero-Shot Policy Adaptation
papers.contribution: Significantly outperforms explicit identification under severe dynamics shifts while improving in-distribution stability and latent interpretability.

papers.title: Escaping the Diversity Trap in Robotic Manipulation via Anchor-Centric Adaptation
papers.contribution: Significantly improves task reliability and success rates over standard diverse sampling strategies under the same budget.

papers.title: Geometry-aware Policy Imitation
papers.contribution: GPI achieves higher success rates than diffusion-based policies while running 20x faster, using less memory, and remaining robust to perturbations.

papers.title: LIMMT: Less Is More for Motion Tracking
papers.contribution: First data-centric study for physics-based humanoid motion tracking demonstrating quality matters more than quantity.

papers.title: Making Learner Weakness Actionable for Learning from Demonstration with Novice Teachers
papers.contribution: CLASP improves success by up to 20% over baselines under the same demonstration budget, improves robustness under distribution shift by 14-20%, and preserves behavioral diversity.

papers.title: MoSA: Motion-constrained Stress Adaptation for Mitigating Real-to-Sim Gap in Continuum Dynamics via Learning Residual Anisotropy
papers.contribution: Achieves superior accuracy and generalization while learning physically meaningful residual anisotropy; validated in sim-to-real robot manipulation.

papers.title: One Demo Is All It Takes: Planning Domain Derivation with LLMs from A Single Demonstration
papers.contribution: Across 1,200 tasks in nine environments, PDDLLM achieves at least 20% higher success rates than LLM-based planning baselines with reduced token costs and successful deployment on physical robots.

papers.title: ROSETTA: Constructing Code-Based Reward from Unconstrained Language Preference
papers.contribution: ROSETTA achieves 87% average success rate and 86% human satisfaction across 116 diverse language preferences on manipulation tasks, outperforming SOTA baselines without extensive offline training.

papers.title: Robust Fine-tuning of Vision-Language-Action Robot Policies via Parameter Merging
papers.contribution: Across extensive simulated and real-world experiments, model merging produces a single model inheriting generalist abilities while robustly learning new tasks, outperforming both pretrained and finetuned models on out-of-distribution variations.

papers.title: Robust Selective Activation with Randomized Temporal K-Winner-Take-All in Spiking Neural Networks for Continual Learning
papers.contribution: RTK-WTA surpasses deterministic K-WTA by 3.07–5.0% accuracy on splitMNIST and splitCIFAR100, enhancing inter-class margins and robustness through expanded feature space utilization.

papers.title: Translating Flow to Policy via Hindsight Online Imitation
papers.contribution: Achieves more than 2× performance improvement over base policy; enables policy acquisition from cross-embodiment video data.

papers.title: Wasserstein Geometry-Aware Adaptive Control via Meta-Learning
papers.contribution: Closed-loop tracking on fully-actuated and underactuated nonlinear systems maintains robustness under significant distributional shifts between training and testing.
